intent: Show one file or image as a compact card with its preview, its name and details, its upload state and its actions.
typical_uses: A file or image attached to a message or waiting in a composer before it is sent
One entry of an upload in progress, done or failed

dont_use_when.situation: The visible surface of a text turn in a conversation
A bounded panel of related content that is not a file
A row in a list of similar things, such as a notification or a search result
A short inline label for a file type or a count

instead.target: a native file input or the application's own drop zone
instead.note: The kit ships no file picker; Attachment only shows a file once the application has one, and its `idle` state is a styling of the card, not an input.

mounted_in.container: any parent in the consuming application
mounted_in.note: A single Attachment may stand on its own, outside an AttachmentGroup.

invariants.text: `state` is set once on the root and reaches the parts without being passed again: `idle` dashes the root's border, `error` tints the root's border, AttachmentMedia's plate and AttachmentDescription's text, and AttachmentTitle shimmers while the state is `uploading` or `processing` (read from React context, the rest through attachment.module.css descendant selectors on the root's `data-state`).

The root's padding is set only while an AttachmentContent is its direct child (attachment.module.css `.attachment.size*:has(> .attachmentContent)`); an attachment with no direct AttachmentContent renders with no padding.

The whole-card hover tint applies only while a button or a link is a direct child of the root, as an AttachmentTrigger is (`.attachment:has(> a):hover, .attachment:has(> button):hover`); an AttachmentAction inside AttachmentActions does not turn it on.
The root draws a 1px ring while any descendant has focus (`.attachment:focus-within`), which is the only focus indication an AttachmentTrigger gets, since the trigger sets `outline: none`.

anti_patterns.dont: Let the `error` state's color be the only sign that an upload failed
anti_patterns.do_instead: Say what failed in AttachmentDescription as well; the state adds no text or icon of its own

good.title: A done file with a remove action
A failed upload that says why
good.code:
<Attachment state="error">
  <AttachmentMedia>
    <FileIcon />
  </AttachmentMedia>
  <AttachmentContent>
    <AttachmentTitle>large-export.csv</AttachmentTitle>
    <AttachmentDescription>Upload failed: file is over 20 MB</AttachmentDescription>
  </AttachmentContent>
</Attachment>

bad.title: Title and description placed straight into the root
bad.why: The root pads itself only while an AttachmentContent is its direct child, and AttachmentContent is what lets the title and description shrink and truncate; without it the card renders with no padding.

companions.typed_by: cva(...), returns (props: VariantProps<typeof attachmentVariants> & { className?: string }) => string
companions.description: The class-name builder Attachment uses for its base, `size` and `orientation` classes. It does not set the `data-state`, `data-size` and `data-orientation` attributes the state styling reads, and it provides no state to AttachmentTitle.
